chapter: Looking back: rock, blues, childhood and guitar innovators
title: Blind blues guitarists and rock drawing on the blues
summary: He remembers blind guitarists playing with bottle necks and says rock borrowed from Muddy Waters and other blues players.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: minstrel shows. And -- but any way, at my home we had all kind of records, and I -- all of my time was spent listening to records, to music, music, music, all kinds of music. And I would hear the guys play the guitars, the blind guys play the guitar, and speaking of -- Blues guitar?

Oh, man, that was it. This was just blues guitar. They would play with the - - some of them would play with the bottle top, you know, the neck of the bottle, the glass neck of a bottle over here and it would sound like a Hawaiian guitar. But blues, you know. So I have always appreciated blues, always could play it. You know. So when we say rock and these things, what they have done, they have gone back and drawn from Muddy Waters all of the blues entertainers and singers. This is all they are doing any way. You know, this is what they are doing, and so they've made money on it.
Plus the wawa, you know. So any way, I don't make a -- that's not my life's work, of course, you know, but as I say, I liked to do it.
